name: Framingham
headline: Several old centers, one city,
on the road and rail line west of Boston.
answer: Framingham is a city of 72,362 people (2020 Census) in Middlesex County, on the main western corridor out of Boston. It grew from separate centers, including Saxonville, Framingham Centre and South Framingham, and its housing runs from mill-era double houses to two-families and suburban homes. Framingham station serves the Framingham/Worcester Line, and the Massachusetts Turnpike crosses the city.
overview: Framingham never had a single village at its heart. John Stone settled near the Sudbury River falls in 1647 and built a gristmill there, the start of what became the mill village of Saxonville. The town was incorporated in 1700, and Framingham Centre grew up as the civic focus on the old Boston turnpike. When the Boston and Worcester railroad reached South Framingham in 1834, that area became the industrial center. Voters approved a city charter in 2017, and Framingham became a city on January 1, 2018.

Those separate centers still shape the map. Saxonville keeps mid-1800s mill housing near the falls, and the Framingham Centre Common Historic District holds 28 buildings around the old common, including the Village Hall and First Parish Church. The Danforth Art Museum and School is now part of Framingham State University. Green space comes in several forms: Callahan State Park has more than 800 acres and seven miles of marked trails, Garden in the Woods shows New England native plants on 45 acres, and the Cochituate Rail Trail runs from Concord Street toward Natick.

Downtown, around the Concord Street common and the rail station, is where the city has zoned for denser housing. Town Meeting approved a Central Business (CB) district there in 2015, and in December 2024 the mayor submitted it to the state as Framingham's district under the MBTA Communities law. The state granted conditional compliance on January 22, 2025, and the city announced full compliance in July 2025; the state's compliance list, as of October 21, 2026, includes Framingham. Projects downtown include Alta Union House, 196 apartments across Concord Street from the Downtown Common, which opened in July 2019, and 181 homes at 358 Waverly Street, about 500 feet from the commuter rail station, where ground was broken in late 2025. The city's 2026 to 2030 Consolidated Plan records a call from local stakeholders for more "missing middle" housing types.

housing.text: The Massachusetts Historical Commission's survey of Framingham records central-chimney double houses built for mill workers at Saxonville around 1825 to 1835, wood-frame tenements and row houses in South Framingham and Coburnville, and two-family houses that became common there in the early 1900s, with relatively few three-deckers. Larger suburban houses were built around Framingham Centre on Park Street, Prospect Street and Salem Road. The city's 2026 to 2030 Consolidated Plan counts 15,318 owner-occupied and 12,492 renter-occupied homes, and 93 percent of the owner-occupied homes are single-unit houses. Seventy-seven percent of the housing stock was built before 1980, and the largest share, 21 percent, dates from 1950 to 1959 (American Community Survey, 2018 to 2022).

villages.name: Framingham Centre
villages.line: The historic civic center around the old common, with large older houses on hillside streets near the Sudbury River.

villages.name: Saxonville
villages.line: The former mill village at the Sudbury River falls in northern Framingham, where mid-1800s workers' housing remains.

villages.name: South Framingham
villages.line: The railroad and industrial center that grew up on the Boston line, with Farm Pond to its south.

villages.name: Coburnville
villages.line: A former industrial and residential area near South Framingham with tenements and two-family houses.

villages.name: Nobscot
villages.line: An area in the north of the city named for Nobscot Hill, on the old road toward Sudbury.

villages.name: Salem End
villages.line: A western area reached by the old roads from Framingham Centre.

commute.text: Framingham station, on Waverly Street, is a stop on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line between Worcester and South Station in Boston. The Massachusetts Turnpike, Route 9 and Routes 30, 126 and 135 all pass through the city.

places.name: Callahan State Park
places.line: More than 800 acres of fields, ponds and seven miles of marked trails for hiking, riding, biking and cross-country skiing, at 1048 Edmands Road.

places.name: Garden in the Woods
places.line: Native Plant Trust's 45-acre botanic garden of New England native plants at 180 Hemenway Road.

places.name: Danforth Art Museum and School
places.line: An art museum and school that opened in 1975 and joined Framingham State University in 2018.

places.name: Cochituate Rail Trail
places.line: A paved trail of about 3.3 miles from Concord Street in Framingham to Washington Avenue in Natick.

places.name: Framingham Centre Common Historic District
places.line: The old town common and 28 surrounding buildings, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1990.

places.name: Farm Pond
places.line: A 151-acre great pond in the center of the city, with shore access at Farm Pond Park on Dudley Road along the western shore and a paved boat ramp at the end of Lakeview Avenue.

places.name: Framingham History Center
places.line: Runs three historic buildings around the Centre Common: the Edgell Memorial Library at 3 Oak Street, the Old Academy at 16 Vernon Street and Village Hall on the Common.

places.name: Saxonville falls and mill
places.line: At the Sudbury River falls on Central Street, the control gates and gears of an 1865 dam remain near the Saxonville mill, whose 1858 section still stands by the river.

history.text: John Stone settled near the Sudbury River falls, in what became Saxonville.
Incorporated as the Town of Framingham.
About 130 Framingham militiamen joined the Battles of Lexington and Concord on April 19.
Shoppers' World opened, the second open-air mall in the United States and the first east of the Mississippi.
Became a city on January 1, after voters approved a charter in 2017.

tax.note: Rates from the City of Framingham Assessors Department page ('FISCAL YEAR 2026 Tax Rates'): residential $11.83 and commercial and industrial $23.97 per $1,000. The page lists no residential exemption. Framingham's local access station reported the City Council's November 10 vote at $11.91 and $24.13 (https://www.accessfram.tv/article/framingham-city-council-approves-fy26-tax-rates); the assessor's figures are used as the later, official ones.

search_notes: 'Framingham MA real estate agent' returns agent directories and profiles (RealTrends, Ramsey Solutions, HomeLight) plus real estate attorney listings, with one generic realtor-guide page. 'Moving to Framingham MA' is led by a storage company's blog posts (UNITS) and mover sites (Lugg, All My Sons, MoveAdvisor). Neither search surfaces a sourced guide to the villages, the rail station or the city's history, which a local community page could supply.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Framingham, MA?
faq.a: The median single-family sale price in Framingham was $700,000 in calendar year 2025, up from $655,000 in 2024, across 442 sales (428 in 2024), according to The Warren Group's MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town report.
Yes. Framingham station, at 417 Waverly Street, is on the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line, which runs between Worcester and South Station in Boston.
Framingham Public Schools. Review its profile with DESE.

faq.q: What is the property tax rate in Framingham?
faq.a: For fiscal year 2026, the City of Framingham Assessors Department lists a residential rate of $11.83 per $1,000 of assessed value and a commercial and industrial rate of $23.97 per $1,000.

faq.q: Has Framingham adopted MBTA Communities zoning?
faq.a: Yes. The city used its downtown Central Business district, approved by Town Meeting in 2015. The state granted conditional compliance in January 2025, the city announced full compliance in July 2025, and the state's list as of October 21, 2026 shows Framingham as compliant.
